tools.name: bodesign_route_net2pcb
tools.description: C04 routing: build a netted .kicad_pcb from a KiCad netlist — load+place footprints, assign nets, set copper-layer count / reserved plane layers (LT_POWER, signals stay on outer layers) / default track width, draw the board outline. Board outline semantics: pass board_mm=[W,H] to draw the Edge.Cuts rectangle at exactly (0,0)-(W,H) on ANY strategy (this is the single source of truth and matches the deterministic preplace R_edge boundary); when board_mm is omitted the outline auto-frames from pad extents + 3mm margin. The result reports outline_source='board_mm'|'pad_extent'. Connector pin expansion (one symbol pin -> several pads, e.g. USB-C VBUS -> A4/A9/B4/B9) is caller-overridable via `connectors`={refdes:{net:[pads]}} and applies to any USB-C footprint on ANY refdes (not just J1). Returns placed/nets/pads_assigned/unmapped plus applied_pinmaps and unmapped_connectors (a USB-C/declared connector that matched no net name is reported, not silently skipped); unmapped>0 means a footprint's pad names don't match the symbol (floating part). Footprint search dirs MERGE fp_dirs (project .pretty parents) with stock — a component whose footprint resolves in NONE is reported in dropped_components + ok:false (never silently skipped); expected_components vs placed surfaces the gap (BR_20260729 §B). Placement strategy: 'grid' (default, naive 8mm baseline) or 'deterministic' — electrically-aware pure-python pre-placement (main-IC anchoring, decap/crystal pin-affinity clustering, largest-first greedy per R4, fixed-seed SA) plus R1/R8 post-place checks; returns source-anchored placement_violations, hpwl_mm, anchor and echoed effective params. deterministic REQUIRES board_mm and FAILS FAST on missing footprint geometry — it never falls back to grid.

plane_layers.description: inner copper layers to reserve as power planes (LT_POWER). Accepts 'In1', 'In1.Cu' or 'In1.Cu:GND' (layer[.Cu][:NET]); layer must be In1..In6. An unrecognised spec FAILS LOUD with PLANE_LAYER_UNKNOWN instead of being silently skipped (BR_20260729 §D) — the result echoes plane_layers_applied[{spec,layer,net,type}] as proof each requested plane was really created

fp_dirs.description: project footprint .pretty parent dirs, MERGED with stock (not exclusive); a netlist component whose footprint resolves in none of them is reported in dropped_components with ok:false, never silently skipped (BR_20260729 §B)

connectors.description: {refdes: {net_name: [pad ids]}} explicit connector pin expansion; omit to use the built-in USB-C table for USB-C footprints

strategy.description: placement strategy; default grid (baseline). deterministic = electrically-aware anchoring/clustering/greedy/SA + R1/R8 anchored checks

seed.description: SA seed for strategy=deterministic (default 42); echoed in result.effective

board_mm.description: [width, height] mm board outline — required for strategy=deterministic

tools.name: bodesign_autoroute
tools.description: Autoroute a netted board with Freerouting when java+freerouting.jar are present in the worker; otherwise returns routed=false with the netted board for external routing. NET-CLASS RULES (BR_20260708): pass `netclasses`=[{name,width_mm,clearance_mm,nets?:[exact],match?:[substrings]}] (ORDERED; a net joins the FIRST class that claims it) to inject per-class width/clearance into the exported Specctra DSN — so a 0.5mm-pitch BGA escape region can route at 0.1/0.1mm while signal/power nets keep their own widths, instead of KiCad's single global 0.2mm rule that makes BGA escape impossible. Unclaimed nets fall into a synthesized default class (default_width_mm/default_clearance_mm). Run bodesign_via_in_pad (BGA fanout) BEFORE autoroute so escape stubs exist. Result adds `netclasses` (per-class net counts + DSN-unit widths + dropped-empty warnings) and structured completion (`unconnected`/`complete`) so a router that converged short is visible here, not only at downstream DRC.

passes.description: freerouting -mp: UPPER LIMIT of auto-router passes (default 40). Lowering it buys speed for a weaker search, and the returned `unconnected` then measures the board AND your budget — a throttled run is NOT evidence the geometry cannot be routed. The response echoes passes_limit/throttled and advises re-running at the default before concluding infeasibility.

default_via.description: padstack name (from the DSN's own `(padstack ...)` declarations, e.g. 'Via[0-7]_300:150_um') for the synthesized fall-through class. BR_20260729 §K: on a fine-pitch BGA the VIA size gates layer changes more than track width does — a router that may not open a small enough via cannot reach the inner layers at all, so widening tracks changes nothing. Without this, unclaimed nets were stranded on the board's original via while named classes could each override theirs. Result reports used_vias/declared_vias/undeclared_vias; freerouting silently IGNORES an unknown use_via, so an undeclared name is reported rather than assumed applied.

netclasses.description: ordered per-class DSN rules; a net joins the first class claiming it (exact `nets` or `match` substring)

tools.name: bodesign_autoroute_preflight
tools.description: C04 route-step diagnostic gate (BR_20260708): probe the ee worker for freerouting prerequisites and say EXACTLY what is missing instead of leaving the route step to die on a raw Java HeadlessException. Checks four things: freerouting.jar on disk, java on PATH, a HEADFUL JRE (freerouting v1.9.0 CLI still calls Toolkit.getScreenSize(), so a *-headless JRE lacking libawt_xawt.so throws HeadlessException even under xvfb), and xvfb-run/DISPLAY. Returns {ready, missing:[...], reason, remedy:[...], probe:{...}} — ready=true ONLY when jar+java+headful-JRE+xvfb/DISPLAY are all present. Call this before bodesign_autoroute on a fresh worker; on ready=false do NOT claim a routed board, fix the named gap (or route interactively in KiCad). No arguments. consider: bodesign_kb_query.

tools.name: bodesign_placement_preflight
tools.description: C04 pre-route placement gate (BR_20260708): read a placed .kicad_pcb and fail fast on a doomed floorplan BEFORE routing, from REAL footprint courtyards (no guessing). Two conditions: (1) courtyard_overlap — any two footprint courtyards that intersect (optionally grown by courtyard_margin_mm) are listed in `overlaps` with the measured mm² (route would inherit a wall of clearance DRC — the 65-violation symptom); (2) sheet_under_filled — total courtyard area / usable board area below min_utilization (default 0.40) means everything is crammed into a strip (the 20%% center-strip symptom). Returns passed=true ONLY when zero overlaps AND utilization meets the floor, plus utilization, overlap_pairs, parts/board areas, board_mm (read from Edge.Cuts unless overridden) and human-readable `reasons`. Never mutates the board and never routes: the caller checks passed and, on failure, re-places (strategy='deterministic') rather than routing into overlap. consider: bodesign_kb_query.

tools.name: bodesign_c04_placement_geometry_gate
tools.description: C04 placement GEOMETRY gate (GATE-C04-01..07, c04-entry-freeze section 4.4; distinct from the landed gate.py verb c04_placement_gate): judge a PLACED .kicad_pcb against its .net. 01 parity: refs + per-ref pad/net assignment board vs netlist (missing/extra/mismatch lists; optional expected_ref_count). 02 courtyard: kicad-cli pcb drc courtyards_overlap count; kicad-cli absent or unusable => status unmeasured with a reason, NEVER pass. 03 keepout: any pad/courtyard/footprint bbox touching a keepout box {name,x,y,w,h[,layer]} (x,y = min corner, mm); keepouts=[] is unmeasured, not a vacuous pass. 04 edge margin: courtyard POLYGON vs Edge.Cuts, min distance >= edge_margin_mm (default 0.40), min measured + offenders reported (AABB only for refs listed in aabb_fallback_refs). 05 copper connectivity/Gerber parity: ALWAYS unmeasured here (placement-only). 06 silkscreen: visible reference-designator text box (KiCad 9.0.9 stroke-font model fitted to pcbnew; rotation handled) vs pad bboxes and courtyard polygons on the same side, clearance silk_clearance_mm (default 0.15); glyphs outside the measured table or bold/italic text are listed as unmeasured_items per ref, never skipped; offenders {ref, against_ref, kind pad|courtyard, clearance_mm}. 07 courtyard gap: pairwise courtyard POLYGON distance >= courtyard_gap_mm (default 0.25), smallest three pairs reported. Courtyard polygons are outset by stroke_width-0.005 mm exactly as pcbnew builds them. Returns {ok, gates:{id:{status pass|fail|unmeasured, measured, offenders}}, unmeasured_gates, inputs:{board_sha256, netlist_sha256}}; ok is true only when every measured gate (01-04, 06, 07) passes and never implies copper/Gerber parity. Missing board/netlist/keepouts fields, a footprint without courtyard geometry, or a board without an Edge.Cuts outline => {ok:false, error} fail-fast; geometry is never defaulted. Never mutates the board. consider: bodesign_placement_preflight, bodesign_layout_drc_gate.

tools.name: bodesign_c04_routing_gate
tools.description: C04 routing-class gate R-01..R-08, pure python on the routed .kicad_pcb. R-01 track width per net class (class min width; escape_exemptions [{ref,max_length_mm}] list declared QFN necks under measured.exempt_necks, undeclared necks fail). R-02 vias per layer transition for classes with min_vias_per_transition (class_rules). R-03 pad entry angle / acid trap (flag < min_entry_angle_deg, default 45: 45-degree entries pass; teardrop zones count as fixed only when a same-net teardrop fill covers the exit; unsupported pad shapes unmeasured per endpoint). R-04 pour islands: filled-polygon outer loops touching no same-net pad/via/track (max_island_area_mm2, default 0 = any). R-05 declared pairs only [{a,b,max_len_mm,max_skew_mm}], absent => unmeasured. R-06 copper-to-keepout margin on tracks/vias/fills/pads (keepouts + keepout_margin_mm; owner_ref pads exempt). R-07 min pour neck width: narrowest copper between boundary edges of a filled polygon vs the net's class min track width (offenders: net, layer, neck_width, location). R-08 escape feasibility (pre-route): class min width W + class clearance C (project-file clearance / classes[].clearance_mm / class_rules clearance_mm) must fit between a pad and other-net pads on at least one exit side; offenders {ref,pad,net,class,min_gap_mm,max_feasible_width_mm,exits_examined}; counts toward ok only on a board with no tracks/vias, informational on a routed board. R-03 models custom pads (anchor rect|circle + filled gr_poly/gr_rect/gr_circle union). Net classes: explicit classes argument, else the sibling .kicad_pro net_settings, else board net_class blocks; none naming the nets => explicit error. Anything not computable => unmeasured with reason, never pass. ok = R-01..R-04 + R-06 + R-07 pass (+ R-05 when declared). Does not judge DRC clearance or impedance.

tools.name: bodesign_c02_mesh_gate
tools.description: C02 printable-enclosure mesh gates (DD-19), pure python, per STL part: M-01 nonempty valid mesh (triangle/degenerate/non-finite counts); M-02 half-edge topology after 1e-5 mm vertex weld: manifold (each edge shared by exactly 2 faces), watertight (no boundary edge), consistent orientation (no same-direction twin) and positive signed volume (inverted shell fails); M-03 bbox extents vs expected_bbox_mm within bbox_tol_mm (axis-ordered, no rotation; units assumed mm); M-04 wall thickness: ray from sampled face centroids along -normal, first-hit distance vs wall_min_mm (sampled normal-direction distance, NOT a true minimum thickness; limits are returned in measured.limits; unmeasured unless M-02 passes). Assembly: M-05 board clearance needs board_manifest_path + clearance_min_mm + explicit board_placement_mm [dx,dy,dz] (registration is never guessed) and tests that the extruded board outline vertices sit inside the cavity at >= clearance; translation only, component heights not modelled, necessary-not-sufficient; otherwise unmeasured with a reason, never pass. M-06 chain: c02_manifest_path consumed_board_outline_sha256 == board manifest exported_outline_sha256 (absent => unmeasured). trimesh, if importable, is a cross-check only and never changes a verdict. tools.name: bodesign_emit_multisheet
tools.description: Emit a HIERARCHICAL schematic — one root `.kicad_sch` carrying a sheet block per subsystem, plus one leaf `.kicad_sch` per sheet — from a spec whose components carry an explicit `sheet` field. This is the multi-page counterpart of bodesign_compose_schematic, which always emits ONE flat page no matter how many subsystems the spec describes. ROUTE SELECTION IS BY DECLARATION, NOT BY COUNT: no `sheet` on any component takes the original flat path unchanged; ANY explicit declaration — INCLUDING exactly one distinct sheet name — takes the root+N-leaf path. The two are never equated, so asking for one sheet explicitly is distinguishable from asking for nothing. `sheet` is the ONLY assignment channel: it is never inferred from `group`, from net topology, or from a catch-all, and it is ALL-OR-NOTHING (a partially declared spec raises E_UNASSIGNED_REFS rather than inventing a bucket for the remainder). `group` keeps its cluster meaning and is scoped PER SHEET — the cluster key is the ordered pair (sheet, group), so equal group strings on different sheets are independent clusters. Each sheet name is used VERBATIM as the leaf filename stem and is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ with NO silent sanitization (E_SHEET_NAME_INVALID / E_SHEET_NAME_EMPTY), and a stem equal to project_name is refused (E_SHEET_NAME_COLLISION) because the leaf write would otherwise truncate the root while the file set still looked complete. CROSS-SHEET NETS: a net whose nodes span sheets is emitted on every leaf holding at least one of its nodes, under its own name, forced onto global_label connectivity — same-named global labels on two leaves join into one net (measured on real kicad-cli 9.0.9). No endpoint is ever dropped; node accounting is re-checked against the input and a node whose ref is on no sheet is reported as an orphan warning rather than silently discarded. FAILURE CLEANUP removes ONLY paths this call created: a path that already exists raises E_OUTPUT_PATH_OCCUPIED before anything is written, so a pre-existing user file can never be in the rollback set. `files` lists real files on disk only — a phantom entry raises E_FILES_MANIFEST_PHANTOM rather than shipping a manifest that names something absent. Contract violations return ok:false with a machine `error.code` and files:[] (nothing written), NOT a partial success. Needs KiCad symbol libraries to resolve pins; it does not run ERC — arbitrate the output with kicad-cli or bodesign_export_netlist.

tools.name: bodesign_verify_netlist_fidelity
tools.description: ELECTRICAL-axis gate: compare a design's spec net partition against the FROZEN KiCad `.net` export(s), by node-set (net NAMES are discarded — power ports rename endpoints, so name alignment is unreliable). Netlist-only: it needs no .kicad_sch, no kicad-cli and no emitter, so it adjudicates a frozen deliverable exported anywhere. Catches the defect class ERC is structurally blind to: net FUSION (two nets welded into one reads as FEWER nets and no dangling pins, so ERC looks CLEANER) and its inverse, a cut net. Reports FOUR INDEPENDENT difference axes, never merged: `fused` (nodes that gained peers — short), `split` (nodes that lost peers — open circuit), `node_diff.spec_only` / `node_diff.emitted_only` (a node in one side only), and `nc_wired` (a pin the design DECLARES not-connected that the export wires into a multi-node net — a defect even when the partition otherwise matches, which is why it is not folded into `fused`). READ `status` BEFORE any field: `ok` = parsed >0 nets, every input readable, all five axes empty; `failed` = >=1 axis non-empty; `not-run` = precondition unmet before any read (no spec, or an empty `emitted` list) so NO comparison was attempted; `indeterminate` = `nets_parsed == 0` or an input could not be parsed — set BEFORE comparison and NOT reachable from `ok`, because an empty export and a board with no nets are the same bytes. A spec of single-pin nets against an empty export previously returned a PASS through exactly that hole. A named `.net` that does not EXIST is a separate channel (`ok:false`, code `NETLIST_MISSING`), not `indeterminate`: one sends you to fix a path, the other to inspect the drawing. Same-named nets on different sheets merge only when they SHARE a node (union-find); disclosure fields (`regrouped`, `spec_overlapping_nodes`, `singleton_only_*`) are carried on `ok` as well as on `failed`, because an exemption a reader cannot see is indistinguishable from a check never made. Pure python, runs in core.

spec.description: the electrical SSOT partition: {net_name: [[ref, pin], ...]}. A node may also be the string "REF.PIN". Net names are used only as labels for the classes — the comparison is by node-set, so a name mismatch between spec and export is NOT a finding. A node the spec declares in more than one net makes the spec not-a-partition; that is reported in `spec_overlapping_nodes` rather than raised, because whether those are aliases or a missing component is a design decision.

emitted.description: paths to exported KiCad `.net` file(s). Several sheets may be passed; classes are merged across files by SHARED NODE. An empty list is `not-run` (nothing was read), a listed path that does not exist is `NETLIST_MISSING`, and a path that exists but yields no parseable nets is `indeterminate` — three distinct outcomes that must not be collapsed.

nc_declared.description: pins the design DECLARES not-connected, as [[ref, pin], ...]. Any of these found on a multi-node net in the export is reported in `nc_wired`. Omit it and `nc_wired` is always empty — which means absent, NOT verified-clean.

tools.name: bodesign_readability_gate
tools.description: FORM-axis gate (plan c03_delivery_contract_and_engine_seams WP6): score how a schematic is DRAWN. `gate_axis` is literally 'form' and every report carries `does_not_authorize: [electrical_correctness, fidelity]` as a DATA FIELD in every status, pass and fail alike — because BR_20260905 §8.5.2 measured a change that improved EVERY geometric criterion at once (junctions 5→43, stub share 73.0%→32.7%, subcircuits 3→11) while raising fidelity `moved` from 10 to 67, because it wired an OPEN CIRCUIT. Every threshold here would have gone green on that change. A PASS from this verb authorizes NOTHING about whether the circuit is correct; run `bodesign_verify_netlist_fidelity` for that axis and report both. ⚠ WHAT IT SCORES, and this is the whole of BR_20260906: it scores the `route_stats` of a LIVE COMPOSE — NOT the `.kicad_sch` sitting on disk. There is no `.kicad_sch` reader in this module. Read `scored_subject` before quoting any verdict: `live-compose` (a spec was composed; `source` names it) or `frozen-stats` (frozen numbers replayed with an explicit denominator `n`; nothing was composed). The third enumerated value `on-disk` is RESERVED AND REFUSED (READABILITY_SUBJECT_INVALID) precisely so this verb cannot CLAIM a measurement it cannot make. `not_scored` states the same fact positively: the delivered schematic's readability is `not-run` here, NEVER `failed`. The defect this prevents: a `ratio 0.2222 FAIL` on btdongle read as a verdict on the DELIVERED drawing, while the two populations differ by an order of magnitude (delivered 426 wires / 56 junctions across 3 sheets vs the scored 116 / 6, single sheet). Do NOT confuse `scored_subject` with `measure_run`: the latter is the historical run the THRESHOLDS were calibrated from (identical in every report ever emitted) and carries a spec path that reads like a subject; it is labelled `what` for that reason. THRESHOLDS ARE SCALE-DEPENDENT (task 6.3): junction > 20, stub share < 40%, drawn_subcircuits/N >= 0.50, all pinned on a live-compose run of the real 45-component/27-net btdongle spec — BR_20260905 §8.5.5 measured a synthetic 28/21 corpus reporting an apparent near-miss where the same code on the real board passed clearly, so a synthetic corpus may supplement the acceptance corpus and may never decide it. These numbers do NOT transfer to a hand-drawn sheet without recalibration. Status codomain: `ok` / `failed` (>=1 threshold unmet, `unmet` names which) / `not-run` (no route_stats, or route_stats missing the task-6.0 emissions — absence is NEVER a pass) / `empty` (ran, nothing to score: zero nets, or N==0 so the ratio has no denominator and was not evaluated) / `indeterminate` (the emitter predates task 6.0, so its stats cannot be reconciled against what was drawn). N is spec-derived per DD-09 and reported beside the ratio, so a low ratio is distinguishable from a small denominator. Pure python, runs in core.

route_stats.description: the `RouteStats.to_dict()` from a compose result. null/absent is `not-run`, never a pass. A dict lacking `stub_share` or `drawn_subcircuits` is also `not-run` with `missing_fields` naming them — a missing key is absent input, not a measured zero, and defaulting it to 0 would let 'no stubs were measured' pass the stub criterion.

spec.description: the design spec the stats came from. Supplying it derives N per DD-09 AND sets `scored_subject` to `live-compose` with the spec as its source. Supply either this or `n`; supplying neither is READABILITY_ARGS_INVALID, because N=0 would then mean both 'no eligible nets' and 'the caller forgot the denominator'.

n.description: explicit denominator, to replay a frozen fixture. Sets `scored_subject` to `frozen-stats`: no spec was composed, so this is a DIFFERENT subject and not a weaker form of the same one.

scored_subject.description: override the derived subject. Closed enumeration: live-compose | frozen-stats | on-disk. Normally OMIT it — the derived value comes from the branch actually taken and so cannot disagree with what was scored. `on-disk` is refused (no .kicad_sch reader exists); an unenumerated value is refused rather than coerced.

subject_source.description: evidence for the subject claim. Derived from `spec` when omitted. Passing it EXPLICITLY EMPTY is refused, so 'no source was supplied' and 'the source is empty' never share an output.

tools.name: bodesign_design_suggest
tools.description: Evidence-backed DRAFT suggestion for one pin class — it SUGGESTS, it never DECIDES. Every returned value is computed from a KB rule and stamped with `evidence.kb_object`; `review_required` is true on EVERY path including the ones that suggest nothing, and `committed` is not a member of the status codomain, so no code path can mark a suggestion as adopted (plan c03_delivery_contract_and_engine_seams DD-02). READ `status` FIRST, and note that THREE of its outcomes return zero suggestions for three DIFFERENT reasons: `suggested` = a KB rule covers this class and produced >=1 value, each carrying its own evidence; `no-rule` WITH AN EMPTY `evidence` block = the class has NO KB anchor at all (nothing ran, so no value could exist — distil a rule into KB before expecting an answer here); `no-rule` WITH A POPULATED `evidence` block = a rule DID run and the supplied context named zero pins of that class (ran, nothing to do); `indeterminate` = a rule covers the class but cannot yield a value — either a required electrical input is unresolvable, or (analog-reference today) the anchor states an OBLIGATION without a value. Which classes are answerable is decided by MEASURED KB coverage, not by plausibility: `power` uses control.power.decoupling-pdn-strategy (0.1uF per 2 power pins, ~15uF bulk per 10, placement <=1.25cm, TI SPRABV2, confidence=verified); `analog-reference` maps to step.sch.mcu-adc-frontend-review, whose entire VREF content is the sentence 'VREF/analog-supply pins get required filtering and grounding' — an obligation with NO capacitance, formula or window, so that class returns `indeterminate` with the obligation named rather than the customary 100nF, because attaching a real KB id to a value the object does not contain is worse than no answer. `ground`, `reset-en`, `boot-strapping` and `nc-dnc` returned no class-specific anchor when queried on 2026-09-06 and therefore return `no-rule`; `clock`, `io-gpio` and `high-speed` are served today by the dedicated suggest_* entry points. A malformed call (unknown pin_class, missing pin list) is `ok:false` with code DESIGN_SUGGEST_INPUT_INVALID, NOT a status — a typo teaches you nothing about KB coverage. Deterministic, side-effect free: the input is never mutated and no file is written.

mpn.description: the part this pin belongs to; echoed into the result for traceability. It does NOT select a rule — rules are chosen by pin_class — so an unknown MPN never degrades the answer.

pin_class.description: one of the nine classes from skills/bodesign/stages/c03-ee/references/pinout-to-circuit-method.md:32-47. A class with no KB anchor returns `no-rule` and an empty suggestion list — NEVER a guessed value. An unsupported class is not an error: it is the honest answer that no rule exists.

context.description: per-class inputs. pin_class='power' requires context.power_pins (a list of pin ids — the cap count IS ceil(pins/2), so an absent list has no honest default) and accepts rail, ref, ground_net. pin_class='analog-reference' requires context.vref_pins and accepts ref. A missing required key is DESIGN_SUGGEST_INPUT_INVALID rather than a zero-count answer, because 'you gave me no pins' and 'this part has no such pins' must not share an output.

tools.name: bodesign_check_c03
tools.description: C03→C04 STAGE-ENTRY gate (BR_20260707): deterministic machine check that C03 (EE) delivery is complete BEFORE C04 layout may start — the entry counterpart to check_c04's output gate. Reads the BOM csv (+ optional Pin_Allocation.csv SSOT + frozen_pad_counts) and HARD-FAILS (gate=FAIL, refuse C04 entry) on: R1 BOM schema lint (column-count/quoting breakage, bad status enum, duplicate (board,ref)); R2 readiness (any draft/blocked row; a finalized row whose mpn carries TBC/TBD/UNDECIDED); R3 drawability (every row needs a symbol-source marker: official|vendor+LCSC|manual|N-A); R4 SSOT crosscheck (active parts U/J/Y/SW must appear in Pin_Allocation.csv — catches the U4 wireless-scheme conflict class; J_* pad counts must match frozen_pad_counts when provided); R5 BOM<->netlist (every BOM row must exist as a drawn symbol) and R6 pin-spec polarity, both requiring netlist_path; R7 datasheet-mandated passives (an adjustable buck missing its feedforward cap / FB divider — an ABSENT PART, which no connectivity rule and no ERC can express) and R8 switch-node shorts (a switching or feedback pin sitting on a power rail — electrically LEGAL, so ERC is silent while the converter is destroyed), both requiring netlist_path with pinfunction annotations; PC-001 passive completeness (an active IC whose power rails carry ZERO rail→GND decoupling — a pinout-only placement that cannot physically work, and that passes ERC, DRC and every connectivity rule; relocated into this delivery path by plan c03_delivery_contract_and_engine_seams DD-01/DD-08, reported under passive_completeness, PRESENCE only and subject set selected by a U* refdes-prefix proxy, with ICs whose supply pins could not be identified named in ics_without_identifiable_rail rather than folded into the green). stock=0 is a non-blocking warn. READ not_checked FIRST: it is ALWAYS non-empty, in BOTH pass and fail, and lists the defect classes this gate structurally does NOT examine (decoupling adequacy BEYOND rail→GND presence — PC-001 checks that at least one decoupling cap exists per identified rail, never its value/count/placement; loop compensation, component VALUES, sequencing, thermal, ESD, analog SI). A PASS means 'the wiring agrees with the paperwork', NOT 'this circuit is correct' — two board-killing defects once passed every rule AND ERC and were caught only because a human happened to read a datasheet (BR_20260802). Each of R4–R8 also reports status='run'|'not_run' so a caller can never mistake 'never looked' for 'looked, clean'. Fail-fast on absent/empty inputs (BOM_MISSING/BOM_EMPTY/PIN_ALLOC_MISSING). Gate values NEVER relaxed to pass (check_c04 floating-PSRAM false-pass lesson). Pure python, runs in core.

netlist_path.description: KiCad .net export(s) covering the schematic(s) this BOM is drawn in, as an ARRAY of paths. A single bare path STRING is still accepted at runtime (back-compat) — the schema is deliberately NARROWER than the runtime, because declaring the union is what BREAKS multi-value calls: an anyOf argument gets serialised to TEXT by MCP clients, so ['a.net','b.net'] arrives as one impossible path and R5/R6 die on NETLIST_MISSING (BR_20260730b §P; proven by A/B in ONE request — covers_boards, a plain array, survived while this argument did not). ENABLES R5 (every BOM row must exist as a schematic symbol) and R6 (BOM pin-spec vs wiring polarity). WITHOUT it both rules are skipped and the report carries netlist_crosscheck.status='not_run': a gate=PASS then does NOT mean every part is drawn, it means nobody looked (BR_20260730 F2 — a verdict must carry the scope that produced it).

covers_boards.description: which `board` column values the supplied netlists actually cover, e.g. ['PRODUCT','CORE']. A product BOM spans every board while one .net covers one schematic, so rows on a board with NO netlist have no baseline and are reported under rows_unassessable_board_not_captured rather than as findings. Omit and coverage is INFERRED from which refs resolved — an inference that cannot tell 'no netlist covers this board' from 'every row on it is undrawn', so the report always states which mechanism was used (board_coverage_basis). Declaring it NARROWS the exempt set but can never WIDEN it past what was observed: a board these netlists actually draw stays assessable even if you omit it here, and the contradiction is reported under board_coverage_conflicts (BR_20260730b §Q — otherwise this argument is a mute button that turns the gate green).

tools.name: bodesign_vault_queue
tools.description: Server vault knowledge queue: components with open knowledge gaps ranked by DD-9 priority (usage frequency x gap severity). The 'what to research next' worklist. Contract identical to GET /vault/queue.

tools.name: bodesign_vault_diagnostics
tools.description: Diagnose the live server-side Component Vault through the supported storage boundary: reports configured vault dir, db presence/size, queue_count, queue preview, and the safe compose-run diagnostic command. It never falls back to a temporary vault or Docker host volume path. Contract identical to GET /vault/diagnostics.

tools.name: bodesign_analyzer_selfcheck
tools.description: Deployment self-check for the C06 analyzer engines (kicad/spice/emc): per engine reports engine_resolvable (the analyzer SCRIPTS are bundled + resolvable via BODESIGN_*_SKILL) and binary_present (kicad-cli / ngspice on PATH), plus can_run, resolved_path, image_role (monolith/ee/core), and all_runnable. Answers 'can simulate/analyze_emc/analyze_thermal actually run in this process?' without a docker exec probe. Distinguishes a missing engine script (would cause skipped-no-skills) from a missing binary (skipped-no-simulator). EE-group: runs on the monolith locally, or forwards to the bodesign-ee worker; the lean core reports image_role=core (engines absent by design — it forwards EE).

tools.name: bodesign_kb_query
tools.description: READ-ONLY, no side effects: query bodesign's self-shipped PCB-design domain KB (the repo ragbase store — distilled, evidence-graded design rules, IPC tables, derating curves, EMC/SI failure modes, workflow controls). Query semantics: whitespace tokens ≥3 codepoints run over FTS; by default a multi-word query is OR-ranked (bm25) so an in-store object reachable by one word is not dropped when a co-occurring word is added (matchMode 'fts-or') — pass mode='all' for exact conjunction (matchMode 'fts-and'). Short CJK tokens (<3) → LIKE scan over title/body, score=0, recency-ordered ('like-scan'); mixed → 'hybrid-or'/'hybrid-and'. Payload always carries matchMode (0 hits is self-describing), hits[] (id/type/title/score/confidence/source_weight) and total. Fail-fast: missing/unmounted KB → KB_UNAVAILABLE + remedy, never empty hits masquerading as no knowledge. Call before judgment-heavy design steps (layout, EMC, SI, derating); bodesign_kb_get(id) returns a hit's full body.

mode.description: multi-word FTS combination: 'any' (default, OR-ranked recall) or 'all' (exact AND conjunction)

tools.name: bodesign_kb_get
tools.description: READ-ONLY, no side effects: fetch ONE domain-KB object's full distilled body (body_md) plus evidence grading (confidence, source_weight) and provenance (its distilled_from/extracted_from lineage edges with per-edge source_weight). Unknown id → KB_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND (consider: bodesign_kb_query to find the right id).

tools.name: bodesign_cache_provision
tools.description: Provision (find-or-mint, idempotent per owner+subject) a per-deliverable WebDAV working cache. Returns the cache token, the /dav/{token}/ mount URL, and host_provision (explicit per-host provision state — decide webdav-mount vs stage-inline from this field). Set issue_webdav_credential=true to ALSO mint the owner's WebDAV Basic credential: the password is returned plaintext ONCE and ROTATED on every issuance (stored salted-hashed; rotation invalidates the previous password, so don't re-issue under a live mount). Default payload carries NO credential. soft_cap is a WARN-FIRST per-owner usage signal; it never blocks. Mount with rclone/davfs2 (class-2 DAV), let heavy tools read/write the same namespace, then bodesign_cache_export + bodesign_cache_close.

issue_webdav_credential.description: opt-in: mint+rotate the owner's WebDAV Basic credential and include it in the payload (R14.6)

tools.name: bodesign_cache_export
tools.description: Export (land) a deliverable cache's whole tree to an absolute host-visible target directory and stamp last_export_at (the close dirty-gate reference). The target's PARENT must already exist — ancestors are never auto-created and no alternative target is guessed (typed EXPORT_TARGET_UNREACHABLE otherwise). Cross-owner access returns typed CACHE_FORBIDDEN. `cache_token` is the cache token from bodesign_cache_provision (do NOT pass it as the generic file-model `token` arg).

tools.name: bodesign_cache_close
tools.description: Close a deliverable cache and free its namespace. Dirty-gated: files modified since the last export return typed WORKSPACE_CLOSE_DIRTY plus the unexported list unless force=true (which discards them). Cross-owner access returns typed CACHE_FORBIDDEN.
